src: A 34-year-old nulliparous woman at 36 weeks of gestation was admitted with severe preeclampsia and underwent an emergency caesarean section.
Postpartum haemorrhage after vaginal delivery was caused by uterine atony and was controlled with oxytocin and a Bakri balloon.
Transvaginal ultrasound showed a complete placenta previa with signs of placenta accreta in a woman with two previous caesarean sections.

src: Placental abruption and retained placenta are leading causes of maternal morbidity in our delivery room.
Preterm birth before 34 weeks was reduced after antenatal corticosteroids and tocolysis in women with threatened preterm labour.
The first-trimester combined test includes nuchal translucency, free beta-hCG and PAPP-A.
Fetal growth restriction was diagnosed when the estimated fetal weight was below the 10th percentile with absent end-diastolic flow in the umbilical artery.

src: Induction of labour with a Foley balloon was offered to women with a Bishop score of 6 or less.
The newborn had an Apgar score of 8 at one minute and a birth weight of 2,400 g, and skin-to-skin contact was started in the delivery room.
A ruptured tubal ectopic pregnancy was treated by laparoscopic salpingectomy.
Women with symptomatic uterine fibroids underwent laparoscopic myomectomy or total laparoscopic hysterectomy.
Deep infiltrating endometriosis and ovarian endometrioma are common causes of chronic pelvic pain and dysmenorrhoea.

src: After controlled ovarian stimulation and oocyte retrieval, a single blastocyst was transferred in a frozen embryo transfer cycle; the clinical pregnancy rate was 45%.
Patients with polycystic ovary syndrome received letrozole for ovulation induction; ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome did not occur.

src: Radical hysterectomy with pelvic lymph node dissection was performed for early-stage cervical cancer.
Low birth weight and preterm birth were more common in twin pregnancies.
